Best 5 Broker Comparison Platforms for Beginners

Best 5 Broker Comparison Platforms for Beginners

GET THE LATEST NEWS
Todays other news
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:31
Instaread

Property professionals are used to comparing services carefully, whether that means weighing up software, insurance, suppliers or financial products. Choosing an investment platform is no different: the right option can depend on everything from fees and available markets to how much guidance a user needs. 

For beginners, that choice can be particularly difficult. Broker websites often present similar features in very different ways, making it hard to judge which platform offers the best value, the clearest information or the most suitable level of support.

Here, we look at five options that can help new investors compare providers and choose a platform that suits their needs.

BrokerChooser – Best overall for beginner broker research

BrokerChooser takes our top spot for beginners because it combines detailed broker comparisons with a relatively straightforward way to narrow down the available options.

The platform has been operating since 2016 and says it now helps more than 7 million investors each month. 

Its research is based on first-hand testing rather than broker specifications alone: analysts open real accounts, deposit their own money and use the platforms themselves before assessing areas such as fees, safety, account opening, deposits and withdrawals, customer service and trading platforms.

BrokerChooser research at a glance:

  • 7M+ investors helped each month
  • 100+ brokers and investment platforms tested and ranked
  • Around 1,200 data points assessed per broker
  • 170,000+ verified criteria across its database
  • 43,000+ risky or unregulated entities tracked in its scam broker directory

Why it works for beginners: BrokerChooser combines extensive broker data with practical comparison tools, making it easier to understand the differences between providers and create a shortlist based on individual needs.

XTB – Best for learning while getting started

XTB combines its investing and trading platform with a substantial range of educational resources, making it an option worth considering for beginners who want to learn as they go.

The broker offers a broad library of learning materials covering investing, trading, market analysis and risk management. This gives newer investors a way to build their understanding while also getting familiar with the tools and features available on a live investment platform.

XTB at a glance:

  • Beginner-focused educational resources
  • Investment and trading guides
  • Access to multiple financial markets
  • Web and mobile trading platforms
  • Market analysis and research tools

XTB’s educational content is supported by practical features such as market news, analysis tools and access to a range of investment products. This can help beginners build their knowledge over time without moving to a more advanced platform right away.

Why it works for beginners: XTB gives newer investors access to educational content, research tools and a live investing platform in one place, making it easier to understand how markets work and gain practical experience.

The Investors Centre – Best for straightforward guides

The Investors Centre is a useful option for beginners who prefer simple explanations and accessible comparisons over highly technical broker analysis.

The website publishes reviews, comparisons and guides covering brokers, investment platforms, ISAs and other financial products. Its content is generally easy to follow, making it a practical starting point for people who are still getting familiar with investing terminology and the differences between providers.

The Investors Centre at a glance:

  • Broker and platform comparisons
  • Investment app reviews
  • Stocks and shares ISA guides
  • Beginner-focused investing content
  • Explanations of fees, features and account types

The Investors Centre takes a more editorial approach to broker research. This can make its content easier to digest, but it does not offer the same depth of first-hand testing or large-scale data analysis as BrokerChooser, which assesses brokers across around 1,200 criteria and maintains over 170,000 verified data points.

Why it works for beginners: Its clear guides and simple comparisons make the basics easy to understand.

IG – Best for beginners who want room to progress

IG is an established trading and investment platform with a broad range of educational resources, research tools and market access.

The platform caters to both newer and more experienced investors, which can make it a good fit for beginners who want something they can continue using as their knowledge develops. Its learning resources cover trading basics, risk management, market analysis and more advanced concepts.

IG at a glance:

  • Educational courses and trading guides
  • Market news and analysis
  • Web and mobile trading platforms
  • Wide range of markets and investment products
  • Research and charting tools

IG offers more features than many beginners will need at first, but that can be useful for users who want to gradually explore more advanced tools and markets over time.

Why it works for beginners: IG offers plenty of learning material at the start, with a wider range of tools and markets as users gain experience.

InvestEngine – Best for straightforward ETF investing

InvestEngine is a streamlined investment platform built primarily around ETFs and long-term portfolio building.

Its narrower product range can make the platform easier for beginners to understand, especially those focused on diversified investing rather than active trading across multiple markets.

InvestEngine at a glance:

  • ETF investing
  • DIY and managed portfolio options
  • Portfolio-building tools
  • Simple web and mobile platform
  • Designed primarily for long-term investing

InvestEngine keeps the investing experience relatively simple. Beginners can choose their own ETFs through its DIY option or use a managed portfolio if they prefer a more hands-off approach.

Why it works for beginners: InvestEngine offers a relatively simple route into ETF investing, with both self-managed and managed options available depending on how involved the investor wants to be.

How to choose the right broker comparison platform?

The best platform will depend on what you actually want to do. A beginner who mainly wants to learn the basics may value educational resources, while someone interested in long-term investing may prefer a simpler platform with fewer products and clearer portfolio-building tools.

It is worth comparing several providers before signing up, paying particular attention to:

  • Fees and charges
  • Available investments
  • Ease of use
  • Educational resources
  • Regulation and investor protection
  • Whether the platform suits your long-term goals

The same principle applies when choosing any service provider, whether that is an investment platform, insurer or even a letting agency: the cheapest or most recognisable option is not automatically the best fit. Look at the service as a whole and make sure you understand what you are getting before committing.
